tasks.description: State may cross a boundary only as a contribution the receiving node can verify and judge. This contract defines the signature and admission block of the operation envelope of PG-04.1 and the node's own admission: verify the signature (the role key of MEM-145 through the same ssh-keygen path, offline), check authority and policy for the scope and classification, then append; a failed step records a rejected event in the vault's operation log through the OpLog API and appends nothing of the payload. Replay is refused through a sequence per sender and scope whose high-water mark is persisted through the operation log, so it survives a restart (the restart rule of SR-1.03), and every Admission reads the log again when it has moved, from the record after the last one it read, so that no two Admissions over one log admit one sequence. A signature proves a key signed; authority is a separate check. The external admission service of SO-F-08 runs before this step when configured. The classification field's values are constrained later by the classification schema of SO-F-05.

title: SO-F-03.4 Contribution signature and two-step admission: a signed, scoped, classified contribution built on the operation envelope, admission into the node's own operation log, replay refused across restarts, and authority checked apart from the signature
request: Version 4 of this spec, which supersedes SO-F-03.3 (signed as contract k-so-f-03-3-contribution-s-0bb27e, built in pull request #358; the SO-F-03.3 spec file is unchanged and stays on record, and the manifest and RECONCILIATION mark it superseded by this spec). Unsigned: a delta proposed for red-team review in pull request #374. Reason: the red-team review of pull request #374 and the owner decision of 1 Nov 2026 that the replay sequence is per sender and scope, one Admission per scope. SO-F-03.3 keeps the high-water mark per sender across all scopes, in memory, read from the log once when the Admission is made and never again. Two things follow, both read and run in a scratch script outside the repository at 042d727: (1) a second Admission over the same log, even a bare new Admission(...) that nothing else knows of, has a stale mark and admits a sequence that another Admission has already admitted, so the log holds it twice; (2) with one Admission per scope over one log, whether a sequence is a replay depends on when each Admission was made, live and after a restart. Changes from SO-F-03.3: (1) the mark is kept per sender and scope; highWater(sender, scope) takes the scope, which defaults to the scope the Admission holds, so every existing call highWater(sender) keeps its meaning; the scope of a stored record is the scope in its stored envelope (rec.data.envelope.extension.contribution.scope), and a stored record that has no usable scope or no usable sequence moves no mark and throws nothing; the key is a structured pair of the sender and the scope and never a plain join of its parts, so two pairs whose joined text would be equal keep their own marks. (2) The Admission reads the log again, incrementally: before the replay check and in highWater it reads with the log's own iterate({ fromSeq }) from the record after the last one it has read, and it does not read at all when the seq of the log has not moved; an append of its own moves the cursor to that record only when its seq is the last seq read plus 1, the very next record, and otherwise the cursor stays where it was and the next read starts at the last seq read plus 1, so that a record another Admission appended in between is still read (a cursor that jumped to every own append would skip it and admit a sequence twice); a log with no numeric seq is read from the record after the last one read each time. That closes both the second Admission over the same log, bare or not, and the order dependence, at the root. (3) Two criteria pin the scope: a message replayed into a different scope is refused (its scope is inside the signed bytes, so the Admission of the other scope refuses it at the signature step), beside the check that the same message again in its own scope is a replay. (4) The reason of the code external_failed, which a hook that throws gets, is fixed text and no longer repeats the message of the throw, which can carry text of the payload; the code, the step and the event are unchanged, and the test at test/federation-admission.test.mjs:320 asserts only ok, step and code, so it stays green. (5) The text that still says per sender is brought in line: docs/FEDERATION.md (the field table row of the sequence and the paragraph after the two steps), docs/schemas/contribution-v1.json (the description of sequence), the head comment of src/engine/federation/contribution.mjs, the head comment of src/engine/federation/admission.mjs and docs/OPERATION-ENVELOPE.md (every line that says it: the SO-F-03 bullet of What other contracts add and, once pull request #381 lands, its Contributions. bullet), by edits to comments and prose only; a command criterion fails on any of the stale phrases and requires the new one in each file. Criterion 2 of SO-F-03.3 (its statement says the per-sender high-water mark) is superseded by the criterion that takes its place here, at the same position and with the same named test; every other criterion of SO-F-03.3 is carried with its statement verbatim…
